speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information with regard to the data security incident involving the personal data of about 655,000 members of a shopping loyalty programme operated by a luxury resort operator in Singapore (a) whether the incident was reported to the authorities and, if so, when was it reported; and (b) what was the reason provided to the authorities for the three-week delay in notifying affected members.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) requires all organisations to put in place reasonable security measures to protect the personal data in their possession or control, to prevent unauthorised access, disclosure or modification.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Guide on Managing and Notifying Data Breaches under the PDPA sets out clear timelines and requirements that organisations must comply with.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Member may ask why notifications are not required to be made immediately.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That is really because in the usual follow-up to the discovery of a data breach, there are usually four things that we would like the organisations to undertake.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First is that they must immediately seek to contain the breach.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The second is that they must then make best efforts to assess the degree and the extent to which the data breach has resulted in loss of data.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The third is then they must assess whether this falls within the requirements for notification, and if it does, then they must proceed to make the report.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And the fourth is that they must then evaluate their containment efforts, whether they are secure.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, there are these four steps, and because the priority is on containment and assessment, PDPC does give the organisation a little bit of time before they make the notification report to the PDPC.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: PDPC will provide their findings in due course.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have a few supplementary questions in relation to that.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Thirdly, this is in relation to whether the Ministry or the PDPC would consider it necessary to impose further specific or enhancement of obligations to these organisations that possesses large volumes of personal data, for example, through licensing conditions, where applicable?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to how long that will take, it goes to the complexity of the investigations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, it is difficult to say in advance what the duration is likely to be.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Her second question relates to whether there were any follow-ups from affected members of MBS.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Essentially, they wanted to draw the PDPC's attention to this, in case it was not notified, or it was not yet aware of the breach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And the second is that they also asked that the PDPC take MBS to account for this breach which, of course, the PDPC intended to do in any case.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This was the extent of the breach that the MBS was able to ascertain.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It further provided advice to the affected members on how they could safeguard their accounts with MBS, as well as other kinds of personal information.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As a responsible measure, they provided a contact for follow-up enquiries, in case the affected members wanted to clarify on various other aspects.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Soh's third question had to do with the organisations that could be in possession of large volumes of data.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our position today already states that a higher standard of personal data protection is required when organisations hold large quantities of different types of personal data or hold data that might be more sensitive, such as insurance, medical and financial data.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In such cases, organisations are required to implement enhanced data protection practices as stipulated in the PDPC's guide to data protection practices for information and communications technology (ICT) systems.
